newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - May 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - May 10.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
The seventh parliament goes into its fourth session on Saturday.
At least 10 people were injured in a gunbattle between two rival groups of students in the Dhaka University campus on Friday.
The fourth round of peace talks between the governmment and the tribal Shanti Bahini rebels begins in Dhaka on Sunday.

Opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) leader Begum Khaleda Zia on Friday said she would launch a "tougher" anti-government agitation programme after the on-going Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) examination.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina on Friday asked her party MPs to alert people against "conspiracy to create artificial political crisis" in the country by a political party.
Bangladesh will receive $210 million as grant assistance from the United States for its health and population programme.
A drought in two major producing countries could be a boon for Bangladeshi tea during the current year.
Director General of the UN Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO), Jacques Diouf, will be visiting Bnagladesh from May 10 to 12.
